channel.title: thrash-metal on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in thrash-metal on Loud Legends

item.title: The Metallica Megahit Classic That 'SUCKS', According To JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: In a not-so-recent behind-the-scenes video, Metallica fans got an unexpected moment: James Hetfield, frontman of one of the most famous metal bands on the planet, didn’t hold back when asked about one of the group’s earliest hits.

item.title: When DAVE MUSTAINE Was Surprised By METALLICA's JAMES HETFIELD: 'I Didn't Think He Knew How to Play'
item.description: Dave Mustaine didn’t always see James Hetfield as a guitarist. In fact, the first time he saw Hetfield pick up a guitar, he was genuinely surprised. The Megadeth frontman shared this moment in a 2023 interview with Metal Hammer, reflecting on the early days of Metallica, long before either band became a household name in heavy metal.

item.title: 'It Scared The @#$% Out Of Me': JAMES HETFIELD Reveals The Real Story Behind METALLICA’s Darkest Song
item.description: Metallica’s frontman James Hetfield has never shied away from heavy topics. Over the decades, he’s written lyrics about death, addiction, war, and emotional isolation. But there’s one track in particular that stands out to him as the band’s darkest.

item.title: The One Musician JAMES HETFIELD Believed Was Just 'Too Good' For METALLICA: 'No Way He’s Going To Join Us'
item.description: When Robert Trujillo joined Metallica in 2003, the band wasn’t just looking for a good bassist. They needed someone who could match their work ethic, play with power, and bring stability after years of lineup changes and creative friction.

item.title: The Controversial Reason METALLICA Members Didn’t Like JASON NEWSTED, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: In a revealing interview from 2018, Metallica frontman James Hetfield opened up about a difficult chapter in the band’s history: their treatment of bassist Jason Newsted, who joined the group following the death of Cliff Burton in 1986.

item.title: JOHN BUSH Explains Why He Rejected METALLICA: 'They Were Nobodies Back Then'
item.description: John Bush, best known for fronting Armored Saint and later Anthrax, recently spoke in depth about the time he was offered a spot as Metallica’s lead singer.

item.title: The Words JAMES HETFIELD Waited Decades To Say Onstage To BLACK SABBATH At Their Final Show
item.description: Metallica showed up in full force at Back to the Beginning, a farewell event held on July 5 at Villa Park in Birmingham, England. The show was designed to mark the final chapter for Black Sabbath as a live band, as well as the last-ever solo performance by Ozzy Osbourne.

item.title: The Songs METALLICA Chose to Say 'Thank You' to BLACK SABBATH in Front of 40,000+ Fans
item.description: Metallica showed up loud, fast, and full of gratitude at Black Sabbath’s final concert, delivering a powerful six-song set that included two unexpected tributes to the band that helped create heavy metal.

item.title: Watch OZZY OSBOURNE and BLACK SABBATH Reunite for Final Performance at 'Back to the Beginning' in Birmingham
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne gave his final live performance on Saturday, July 5, during the Back to the Beginning event at Villa Park in Birmingham, U.K. The 76-year-old singer took the stage seated on a black throne, delivering a five-song set with his solo band.

item.title: The Legendary Musician Who Made JAMES HETFIELD Rethink His Entire Creative Process
item.description: Even after more than four decades with Metallica, James Hetfield is still learning. The frontman has spoken about what keeps him motivated creatively, crediting an unexpected influence, Elton John, with challenging the way he approaches songwriting and performance.

item.title: The Disgusting Reason Metallica's JAMES HETFIELD Hates LOAD and RELOAD Album Covers
item.description: Metallica’s mid-’90s albums, Load and Reload, are remembered for more than just a shift in musical style. Their cover art caused a stir too, especially with frontman James Hetfield.

item.title: Slipknot, Lamb of God, Anthrax Members Join Comic Con Birmingham Lineup
item.description: Comic Con is coming to Birmingham, and this year’s event will feature more than just movie and TV stars. Several well-known rock and metal musicians are set to appear, including members of Slipknot, Lamb of God, and Anthrax.

item.title: SEPULTURA’s Derrick Green Says His Parents Supported His Music From the Start: 'They Were Very Open-Minded'
item.description: Derrick Green, longtime frontman of the Brazilian metal band SEPULTURA, recently opened up about how his parents reacted when he first started screaming into a microphone. In a new interview with Finland’s Chaoszine (watch below), Green said his parents were “very open-minded” about his decision to become a musician, even when his early performances were loud and intense.

item.title: The Singer METALLICA Wanted Before JAMES HETFIELD, But He Said No
item.description: James Hetfield is the face and voice of Metallica, one of the biggest heavy metal bands in the world. His gritty voice, aggressive rhythm guitar playing, and songwriting skills have helped define the band’s sound since the early 1980s.

item.title: LIMP BIZKIT's WES BORLAND Cosplays As Skull-Faced JAMES HETFIELD At Metallica’s Denver Show
item.description: Limp Bizkit guitarist Wes Borland turned heads at Metallica’s Denver show on Friday by dressing up like a skull-faced version of 1980s James Hetfield (watch below). The look included a “Metal Up Your Ass” t-shirt and white high-top sneakers, all while performing a full 10-song set.

item.title: Megadeth Celebrates 40 Years of 'Killing Is My Business' With Limited Box Set
item.description: Megadeth is marking the 40th anniversary of its debut album with a special box set release. Titled Killing Is My Business… And Business Is Good!, the ultra-limited collection arrives October 17 and will be restricted to just 350 copies.

item.title: KIRK HAMMETT Opens Up About Comparing Himself To New Guitarists: 'Where Did I Go Wrong? I Should Be Much Better'
item.description: Kirk Hammett might have four decades with Metallica under his belt, but if you ask him, he’s not exactly resting on his reputation. In a recent interview with Metal Hammer, the longtime guitarist was asked to reflect on how he sees himself as a player.

item.title: GENE HOGLAN Says METALLICA’s 'One' Echoes DARK ANGEL: 'That Beat Came From Us'
item.description: In a recent interview, Gene Hoglan, drummer for the thrash metal band Dark Angel, shared his thoughts on a long-standing theory among metal fans, that Metallica’s 1988 track “One” was inspired by Dark Angel’s 1986 song “Darkness Descends.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Breaks Down the Goal of New METALLICA Doc: 'Turn The Spotlight Away From Us And Celebrate The Fans'
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich wants people to know the band isn’t the main focus of their new documentary. The real stars, he says, are the fans. Speaking on the red carpet at the Tribeca Festival premiere of Metallica Saved My Life, Ulrich explained why the film shifts attention away from the band and onto the people who have supported them for more than four decades.

item.title: Dream Theater's MIKE PORTNOY Defends LARS ULRICH: 'He Takes a Beating, But He's Invaluable'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for Dream Theater, says Lars Ulrich deserves more credit. In a recent chat with El Estepario Siberiano (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Portnoy explained why he thinks the Metallica co-founder is often misunderstood.

item.title: The Two METALLICA Songs JAMES HETFIELD Finds 'Truly Difficult' To Perform Live: 'Really Messes With Me'
item.description: Metallica has been around for over 40 years, and their music is known for being fast, loud, and often complex. But for frontman James Hetfield, two songs from their 2008 album Death Magnetic still stand out as especially difficult to play live.

item.title: How METALLICA Fooled Audiences in the Early Days, According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'We Took All The Credit'
item.description: Metallica, one of the most recognized names in heavy metal, wasn’t always the arena-dominating force it is today. Back in 1981, when James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich first formed the band, they didn’t have a vault of original songs ready to go.

item.title: Metallica's KIRK HAMMETT Recalls Struggling With 'The Unforgiven': 'I Wasn't Prepared For It'
item.description: Metallica guitarist Kirk Hammett is known for writing some of the band’s most famous guitar parts, but not every one came easy. In a recent interview with Metal Hammer, he opened up about the difficulties he faced while working on the solo for “The Unforgiven”, one of the standout tracks from the band’s 1991 self-titled release, often called “The Black Album.

item.title: MIKE PORTNOY Says LARS ULRICH Was a Major Influence: 'He Was More Than Just a Drummer'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for progressive metal band Dream Theater, recently shared that Lars Ulrich of Metallica had a big impact on his career, and not just behind the drum kit.

item.title: FRANK BELLO Says His Grandmother's Final Show Was ANTHRAX At Yankee Stadium: 'She Loved It'
item.description: Anthrax bassist Frank Bello has shared a personal memory from one of the biggest shows of his career, the Big Four concert at Yankee Stadium in 2011.

item.title: When MAX CAVALERA Almost Reunited With SEPULTURA: 'We'll Cross Paths Again'
item.description: Max Cavalera is best known for helping create one of Brazil’s most influential metal bands: Sepultura. But in 1996, after years of success, he walked away from it all.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says DAVE MUSTAINE ‘Hated Playing Before SLAYER’ On 2010 Tour
item.description: Dave Mustaine wasn’t happy with his spot on the lineup during MEGADETH’s tours with SLAYER, according to former bandmate David Ellefson. In a recent episode of The David Ellefson Show podcast (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH), the former MEGADETH bassist spoke about the 2010 Jägermeister Music Tour.

item.title: The Problem With 'LOAD' and 'RELOAD', According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'I Hate That Part Of Us'
item.description: Metallica made a name for itself in the early days with fast, aggressive thrash metal. But things changed with the release of their self-titled album in 1991, known to most as the Black Album.

item.title: What Growing Up Was Like for DAVE MUSTAINE: 'My Dad Drank A Lot And Was Abusive'
item.description: Dave Mustaine, the founder of Megadeth and one of heavy metal’s most recognizable voices, has lived a life filled with music, fame, and success. But behind the guitars and sold-out shows is a past that’s far less glamorous.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Reveals How the 'Terrible' LARS ULRICH Convinced Him to Start METALLICA
item.description: James Hetfield remembers the first time he met Lars Ulrich. According to him, Lars wasn’t exactly a great drummer when they crossed paths. Still, something about his energy made a lasting impression.

item.title: The Backstage Incident That Made KERRY KING Call a Rock Icon a 'Complete Jerk'
item.description: Not everyone in the world of music gets along, and that includes some of its biggest stars. Even in heavy metal, a genre known for its intensity and larger-than-life personalities, there are musicians who just don’t click.

item.title: The Night SLASH Felt Deep Shame Over GUNS N’ ROSES’ Treatment of METALLICA: 'I Lost Their Respect'
item.description: Back in the early ’90s, Guns N’ Roses were living the full-throttle rockstar fantasy, loud, chaotic, and unapologetic. Their shows were wild, their image untamed, and their reputation built on pushing limits.

item.title: The One Thing That Could End MEGADETH, According to DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Megadeth has been going strong for four decades, led from day one by guitarist, vocalist, and founding member Dave Mustaine. He’s the only constant in the thrash metal band’s long history and the driving force behind many of its best-known songs, including “Peace Sells,” “In My Darkest Hour,” “Holy Wars… The Punishment Due,” “Symphony of Destruction,” “A Tout Le Monde,” and “Trust.

item.title: MEGADETH's DAVE MUSTAINE On the 'Puppy Incident': 'JAMES Got Punched In The Mouth. He Kicked My Dog'
item.description: There’s no elegant way to introduce a story that ends with James Hetfield catching a mouthful of knuckles. Especially when the instigating factor was a puppy. But here we are.

item.title: 'The BIGGEST CLICKBAIT of All Time' Involving Megadeth’s DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Dave Mustaine Sentenced to Life? No, Dave Mustaine isn’t in prison. Yes, people actually believed he was. And of course, someone on YouTube made money off it.

item.title: Sodom's TOM ANGELRIPPER On Modern Metal Production: 'It's Cheap And It Shows'
item.description: Tom Angelripper has no patience for how modern metal is made. From his perspective, today’s studio habits cut corners and it’s obvious. “Recording in a digital way is cheap,” he said (via Blabbermouth).

item.title: Ex-EXODUS RICK HUNOLT Looks Back On Thrash Origins: 'We Inspired METALLICA And SLAYER'
item.description: Ex-EXODUS guitarist Rick Hunolt didn’t bother dancing around it during a recent chat with Pod Scum host Rexx Ruger (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.NET). When Ruger put Hunolt and Gary Holt on the same tier as Hetfield/Hammett or Hanneman/King, Hunolt didn’t blink.

item.title: CHARLIE BENANTE Says BLACK SABBATH Helped Shape ANTHRAX’s Sound: 'We Covered Sabbath Bloody Sabbath'
item.description: Anthrax drummer Charlie Benante pointed to Black Sabbath as a key influence on the band’s formative sound, recalling how their admiration for the Birmingham pioneers led them to cover Sabbath Bloody Sabbath during a formative period in their career.

item.title: The Heavy METALLICA Song That Tells the Story of JAMES HETFIELD’s Childhood TRAUMA
item.description: James Hetfield, guitarist and frontman of Metallica, didn’t exactly grow up riding rainbows. His early years were marked by the rigid dogma of a household that followed Christian Science, a belief system founded by Lafayette Ronald Hubbard (yep, the same guy behind Scientology).

item.title: The GRUNGE Band JAMES HETFIELD Says 'Saved Music': 'It was exactly what music needed'
item.description: Back when rock was drowning in mousse and tight pants, Nirvana kicked down the door like a grunge-splattered SWAT team. Metallica? They’d already been tearing limbs off with thrash riffs from the Bay Area for a decade.

item.title: STEVE DIGIORGIO On Recording With DAVE MUSTAINE: 'He Wasn't What I Expected'
item.description: Steve DiGiorgio, longtime bassist for Testament, has spoken candidly about his brief but intense experience recording with Dave Mustaine for Megadeth’s album The Sick, The Dying… And The Dead!

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD’s Favorite Thrash Bands (That Aren’t METALLICA, SLAYER, MEGADETH or ANTHRAX)
item.description: At this point, saying Metallica “isn’t thrash anymore” is like complaining MTV doesn’t play music videos. Welcome to the last three decades. Sure, the band traded speed for stadiums a while back, but try telling the IRS they’re not the face of thrash metal and see how that goes.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On the 'Weak' METALLICA Member: 'Not Amazing'
item.description: James Hetfield has always been particular when it comes to Metallica’s music. Known for his precision as a rhythm guitarist, he’s often regarded as the most technically sharp member of the band, along with current bassist Robert Trujillo.

item.title: When METALLICA Brought Back 'FRANTIC' Live And JAMES HETFIELD Roasted St. Anger
item.description: Back in 2021, Metallica briefly resurrected “Frantic”, the chaotic opener from their 2003 punching bag of an album, St. Anger. The band pulled the song out of retirement for a set at the Aftershock Festival on October 8 (watch the video below), years after it had mostly vanished from live shows following a few scattered appearances in 2019 and a much longer break since 2011.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Says Younger Fans Ignore METALLICA Classics: 'They're More Into the New Stuff'
item.description: Not every Metallica fan has Master of Puppets tattooed on their brain. According to Lars Ulrich, a surprising number of listeners are skipping the band’s old-school thrash masterpieces in favor of more recent material.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says MEGADETH Took Credit For 'Soldier On!': 'Just Wiped My Name Off'
item.description: David Ellefson isn’t done unpacking his past with Megadeth,and he’s brought receipts. In a new interview with The Delz Show, the former bassist draws some not-so-subtle contrasts between how Metallica handled songwriting credits with Dave Mustaine and how Mustaine allegedly did the opposite when it came to Megadeth’s own track, Soldier On!

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On His Father's Abandonment: 'He Didn't Even Say Goodbye'
item.description: Before the arenas, awards, and global tours, James Hetfield was just a kid growing up in the suburbs of Los Angeles. The setting looked ideal from the outside.

item.title: How LEMMY KILMISTER Helped Invent THRASH METAL With ACE OF SPADES
item.description: By the late 1970s, rock had ballooned into a spectacle of arena shows, towering stage sets, and endless guitar acrobatics. Meanwhile tucked away in sweaty basements and smoky pubs, a small group of musicians were chasing something far less polished.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Recalls METALLICA Audition: 'My Mom Used To Clean Lars' Apartment'
item.description: Dave Mustaine didn’t need to strike a single chord to sense the outcome of his audition for Metallica. After spotting their ad in a magazine, he reached out to Lars Ulrich and arranged to meet up in Newport Beach for a live tryout.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Says FAITH NO MORE's Mike Patton Is 'An Unprofessional Jerk'
item.description: Dave Mustaine has spent over 40 years running the Megadeth machine as guitarist, vocalist, songwriter, and self-appointed keeper of thrash metal’s purity. In that time, he’s built not only an impressive discography, but a side hustle in speaking his mind with the grace of a sledgehammer.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On Metallica T-Shirts: 'I’m Not Sure I Want Them Wearing That'
item.description: Plenty of metalheads have their rituals. They blast albums, whether on vinyl, cassette, or whatever streaming service rules the moment. They pack venues when the tour bus rolls into town.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE starts recording vocals as MEGADETH’s 17th studio album nears completion
item.description: The next Megadeth record has been crawling toward completion for months. Since the release of The Sick, The Dying… and the Dead! back in 2022, work on its successor has quietly advanced.

item.title: What James Hetfield And Robert Trujillo Would Do If Metallica Never Existed
item.description: Episode 98 of The Metallica Report tossed out a simple question that got James Hetfield and Robert Trujillo thinking about an alternate universe where Metallica never happened. The fan-submitted query from Denmark asked them to picture their lives without the band that has basically defined them.

item.title: David Ellefson: "I Miss Dave" But I’m Done With Megadeth’s Drama
item.description: David Ellefson still feels the absence of Dave Mustaine in his life, even after everything. In a recent chat with The Delz Show, Ellefson reflected: “I miss Dave too.

item.title: Kirk Hammett Rules Out Retirement From Metallica Despite 62 Years of Age
item.description: Kirk Hammett has no interest in slowing down. Speaking to Metal Hammer, he dismissed the idea of retirement entirely. “I don’t believe in retirement. Retirement is something that’s been forced onto people; I don’t believe musicians are allowed to retire,” he said.

item.title: James Hetfield Shares The Cost of Fame: ‘They Think They Know Me’
item.description: Metallica’s new documentary, Metallica Saved My Life, made its debut at the Tribeca Festival in New York City on June 11. After the screening, all four band members joined The New Yorker’s Amanda Petrusich for a conversation that pulled back the curtain on both their private lives and the inspiration behind the film.

item.title: David Ellefson Breaks Down Megadeth’s Risk and Its Divisive Legacy
item.description: In 1999, Megadeth rolled the dice with Risk, a record that veered sharply away from the band’s thrash metal identity. For David Ellefson, the album remains, in his own words, “probably the most controversial album in the catalog.

item.title: Megadeth's Bonnaroo 2025 Show Canceled Due to Severe Weather
item.description: Whatever was left of Bonnaroo 2025 got washed straight into the Tennessee mud. What began as a promising four-day event was abruptly halted when severe storms turned Manchester into a swamp, and by Friday night, organizers pulled the plug on the entire weekend.

item.title: Dave Mustaine Confirms Megadeth’s Album 17 Is Taking Shape—205 Songs Under Review
item.description: Alright folks, gather ‘round—Dave Mustaine has spoken. And when Dave speaks, metalheads listen… usually while arguing on the internet about which Megadeth lineup was best. (If you said “Super Collider era,” we need to talk.

item.title: David Ellefson Opens Up About MEGADETH Lawsuit and Band Power Structures
item.description: Okay, so—David Ellefson, ex-MEGADETH bassist, legendary lawsuit haver, and a guy who’s probably had to explain that no, he is not related to Elle Woods from Legally Blonde, just dropped some hot takes about band dynamics.

item.title: Max Cavalera on Re-Recording SEPULTURA’s Early Albums: “They Never Sounded Right”
item.description: Oh boy, here we go. Another “let’s redo our old stuff, but this time better” kind of deal. You know, like when you rewrite a high school essay as an adult and suddenly realize, wow, I really didn’t understand metaphors back then.

item.title: Watch: Marty Friedman Drops Visualizer for “A Prayer” From Drama
item.description: Marty Friedman, the once-and-forever legendary (but now solo and doing his thing) former MEGADETH guitarist, just threw a visualizer our way for his track “A Prayer.” You know, that song from his album Drama?

item.title: Teemu Mäntysaari Discusses Progress on Megadeth's New Album
item.description: Megadeth’s next album? Already in motion. Ideas everywhere, so many good ones, it seems. Guitarist Teemu Mäntysaari, speaking with Megadeth Digital, paints a picture of a band creating across continents.

item.title: Metallica Returns to Australia and New Zealand This November
item.description: Metallica’s unyielding journey continues, with the band slated to storm Australia and New Zealand next November. This leg of their endless ‘M72 World Tour’ has a lineup that’s sure to turn some heads, featuring Evanescence and Suicidal Tendencies as supporting acts.

item.title: James Hetfield: "We Don’t Want to Be a Legacy Band That Only Plays Hits"
item.description: METALLICA’s James Hetfield has made it pretty clear that they’re not interested in simply coasting on past glories. In an interview on “The Metallica Report”—that podcast where the band gives you a peek behind the curtain—James laid it out.

item.title: Cliff Burton's Spirit Lives On in Metallica's Music, Says James Hetfield
item.description: James Hetfield still hears Cliff Burton’s voice. Not literally, but in his head when he’s writing music. During a recent episode of “The Metallica Report”, the frontman was asked if Cliff still influences his work.

item.title: 'Master Of Puppets' Wins Out for Shavo Odadjian in METALLICA Album Showdown
item.description: When Shavo Odadjian, bassist of SYSTEM OF A DOWN, got hit with the impossible question of whether METALLICA’s “Ride The Lightning” or “Master Of Puppets” was the superior album during an interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: Metallica Confirms 2025 Headline Tour with Iconic Support Acts
item.description: Metallica is rolling out a 2025 North American tour, bringing their mix of old-school riffs and new album jams to a lineup that includes Sick New World and Sonic Temple festivals.

item.title: Metallica Pays Tribute to Dedicated Fan Who Died During Edmonton Concert
item.description: Metallica paid a solemn tribute yesterday to one of their own— a dedicated fan, known as Lorne or simply “Viking,” who tragically passed away during their concert in Edmonton, Alberta.

item.title: Metallica’s Ride the Lightning Sales Surge 160% Amid 40th Anniversary
item.description: Calling Metallica one of the biggest-selling bands in music is almost redundant at this point. With albums like the Black Album still lingering on Billboard charts and streaming relentlessly decades later, the band’s impact is as constant as it is undeniable.

item.title: Robert Trujillo Calls Metallica Bass Position the “Most Demanding Gig”
item.description: Robert Trujillo might be the newest face on the Metallica bass, but with two decades under his belt, he’s hardly the fresh recruit anymore. Slotting in as the fourth bassist after Jason Newsted, the legendary Cliff Burton, and, yes, the lesser-known Ron McGovney (check Wikipedia if you must), Trujillo’s view of the job is clear: playing bass for Metallica is no walk in the park.

item.title: James Hetfield’s Pre-Tour Anxiety: “It’s Just Me and a Rubber Guitar”
item.description: James Hetfield of Metallica has his own brand of anxiety dreams, where his worst-case scenarios aren’t about showing up to class unprepared. No, they involve his bandmates vanishing, his guitar turning into rubber, and feeling like he’s the only one taking things seriously while everyone else is in party mode backstage.

item.title: Metallica Wins Best Metal Performance, Only Trujillo Attends GRAMMYs
item.description: Metallica snags the Best Metal Performance GRAMMY, but if you think the band showed up in full force to accept it, think again. As usual, the GRAMMYs treated metal like an afterthought, burying the award for “72 Seasons” in the untelevised dungeon.

item.title: Metallica Sets New Attendance Record at St. Louis Dome; See Details
item.description: Metallica has managed to once again defy expectations by packing out St. Louis’ Dome at America’s Center, showing that even after decades in the game, they’re still pulling crowds that could rival any pop superstar.

item.title: Metallica Files Lawsuit to Halt Bootleg Sales Before St. Louis Concert
item.description: Metallica’s merchandise machine is back at it, keeping the unauthorized sellers in check before they even get a shot at making a quick buck off their name. This time, their touring merch partner, Merch Traffic, has filed a lawsuit in St.

item.title: Metallica Competes for Billboard’s Top Rock Duo/Group Award
item.description: Metallica has snagged two Billboard Music Award nominations this year, a surprising nod from an awards scene that, let’s be honest, usually knows nothing about rock or metal.

item.title: MTV Names Metallica in Best Rock Category for EMA 2023
item.description: Metallica Earns a Nod for an MTV European Music Award—But Don’t Get Too Excited. Since the infamous moment when Jethro Tull snagged a Grammy over Metallica, metalheads everywhere learned that mainstream award shows are, for the most part, a waste of time.

item.title: Metallica’s Classic Albums Return in Limited Colored Vinyl Reissues
item.description: Metallica’s bringing out the big guns with their upcoming reissue series, serving up their classic albums on colored vinyl as if you haven’t bought these a few times already.

item.title: "Stream, Buy, or Steal": Lars Ulrich's Take on Modern Music Fans
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich once wore the crown of “public enemy” in the music scene, especially when he led the crusade against Napster and the whole file-sharing culture. Back then, he was the face of the so-called “greedy musician,” railing against the free-for-all nature of downloading that let everyone grab songs (and viruses) off the internet, slap them on a blank CD, and call it a day.

item.title: Watch: Metallica Drops New “Too Far Gone?” Video with Tour Highlights
item.description: Metallica might’ve dropped 72 Seasons a mere five months back, but the internet reaction could’ve fooled anyone into thinking it’s been years since that release. One side hollered about “disastrous trash,” while the other shrugged, calling it “pretty decent.

item.title: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich on Tour, Streaming Records, and Band Longevity
item.description: Lars Ulrich is no stranger to marveling at Metallica’s unlikely ride to the top. As their colossal M-72 tour rolls on, the drummer recently shared some reflections with FOX 10, and let’s just say, humility is still in the air.

item.title: Metallica Welcomes Unlikely Guest: A Dog Named Storm at LA Concert
item.description: Los Angeles had an unexpected guest at Metallica’s August 25 concert—an adventurous dog named Storm who, without a ticket or invitation, managed to sneak into SoFi Stadium and settle right in with the crowd.

item.title: Metallica’s "Nothing Else Matters" Reaches 1 Billion Streams on Spotify
item.description: Metallica’s “Nothing Else Matters” has now crossed the monumental 1 billion streams mark on Spotify. This track, from the band’s blockbuster 1991 self-titled album, divides opinions like few others.

item.title: Metallica’s M72 Tour Breaks SoFi Stadium’s Single-Show Record
item.description: Metallica just sent Taylor Swift’s attendance record at SoFi Stadium spinning. In a double dose of pure metal, Metallica managed to pull off a weekend showdown that drew fans from every corner, making sure to leave their mark.

item.title: Watch: Exclusive Footage of Metallica's Phantom Lord from Jon Zazula Tribute
item.description: Metallica just dropped official footage of them ripping through Phantom Lord at last weekend’s tribute show for their old manager, Jon Zazula. Yeah, it was one of those nights.

item.title: Watch: Metallica Pays Tribute to Megaforce Founders with Old-School Set
item.description: Metallica recently gave fans a nostalgic kick in the gut with a special throwback show that would make any old-school fan tear up—if they’re still capable of crying, that is.
